description:
Found by the fz-kdt.125 cold review (2026-09-01, probe q2join.fz in
session scratchpad rev125/). Second live P1 wrong answer at base, both
paths (interp AND native):

  P.run(f, x, t) forwards to twice(f, x, _t); called with
  (inc,10,:a) (tri,10,:b) (inc,10,:b) (tri,10,:a)
  means 12 90 12 90 -- base prints 12 90 90 12.

The :a/:b tag splits run/3 into two KEYS; within each key the two
closure literals remain unseparable, so each key's arm 0 takes
everything. This CORRECTS fz-kdt.125's boundary table: 'an extra
discriminable argument -> CORRECT' holds only while each tag maps to
exactly one literal. General statement (stronger than 125's): the
dispatch plan tests the OBSERVABLE columns and then asserts the whole
CORRELATED row; wherever the unobservable column is not functionally
determined by the observable ones, the routing is a lie.

SAME FIX as fz-kdt.125 (the closure-identity predicate axis separates
the literals directly); this ticket exists for its own three-path gate
(q2join lands as a fixture in the 125 build) and its own verification
at close. Blocked by fz-kdt.125.
title: P1: tag-split keys still misroute -- the plan tests observable columns then asserts the whole correlated row
